extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Sounds made by common objects — every object produces a unique sound. A bell rings, a drum beats, a whistle blows, a guitar strums, a car horn honks, a bird chirps. Sound is produced by vibrations. (2) Pleasant and unpleasant sounds — Pleasant sounds: birdsong, soft music, rain, wind in trees, flowing water. These make us feel calm and happy. Unpleasant sounds: traffic horns, drilling, firecrackers, loud machinery, screeching. These make us feel irritated and stressed. (3) Sound as a warning signal — many sounds warn us of danger. Fire engine siren (fire emergency), ambulance siren (medical emergency), police siren (crime emergency), school bell (start/end of class), car horn (alert others), smoke alarm (fire at home), burglar alarm (intrusion). Without warning sounds, we would not know about emergencies. (4) Noise pollution and health effects — Noise pollution is harmful unwanted sound in the environment. Sources: traffic, construction, loudspeakers, factories, firecrackers, aircraft. Health effects: hearing loss, headache, sleep disturbance, stress, difficulty concentrating, high blood pressure. Prevention: use earplugs, plant trees (absorb sound), lower volume on devices, ban loud horns near hospitals and schools, use soundproofing, follow noise rules. Misconceptions: 'only very loud sounds cause hearing damage' (WRONG — long exposure to moderately loud sounds also causes gradual hearing loss), 'noise pollution is not a real problem' (WRONG — noise pollution causes serious health effects like hearing loss, stress, and sleep problems), 'sound has no practical use beyond music' (WRONG — sound is used as warning signals for emergencies like fires, ambulances, and alarms), 'pleasant sounds cannot cause noise pollution' (WRONG — even music at very high volume becomes noise pollution), 'earplugs damage your ears' (WRONG — earplugs PROTECT ears from loud noise and prevent hearing damage).
